    Foundations

    Principles, screen sizes, spacing, radius, colour, type, icons, motion and accessibility, the values every component is built from.01 Design principles · 02 Screen sizes & grid · 03 Spacing · 04 Radius & elevation · 05 Colour & contrast · 06 Typography & numerics · 07 Iconography · 08 Motion · 09 Accessibility
    01

    Design principles

    Six rules, each shown as the wrong version beside the right one. Every one of them is a way of not making the screen busier.

    1 · The system decides, the agent sees why
    ✕ A list to choose from
    1Priya Raghavan
    2Daniel Okafor
    3Meera Shah
    Agent spends 6s deciding, 78× a day
    ✓ One card + a reason
    Priya Raghavan
    Opened pricing twice yesterday
    Agent spends 0s deciding
    The reason line is not decoration, it is what makes a machine-chosen order acceptable to a human. Remove it and agents start skipping cards to regain control.
    2 · Three facts, then a door
    ✕ Everything, always
    Company · Industry · Size · RevenueSource · Owner · Created · StageWebsite · LinkedIn · AddressTags · Score · Last touch · Next
    16 facts, none of them read
    ✓ Three, then more
    Ops Manager · Kirloskar Pneumatic62 employees · PuneAttempt 3 of 6 · last spoke 12 Jul
    Three facts is what an agent can absorb in the 1.5 seconds between the card appearing and the line ringing. The fourth fact is read by nobody.
    3 · Additions must displace
    9
    targets today
    1
    proposed
    1
    must be removed
    9
    still 9
    The console's persistent interactive-target count is capped at 9 and enforced in review. A feature request that cannot name what it displaces is not ready.
    4 · Compliance blocks, it does not warn
    ✕ Dismissible
    Outside calling hours
    ✓ Removed from the queue
    21:14 localreturns 09:00
    Never offered, no decision to make
    A dismissible compliance warning is a compliance failure with extra steps. Anything that must not be dialled is removed from the queue before the agent ever sees it, which also removes the alert from the screen.
    5 · The keyboard is the primary input
    ␣dial1–7dispositionNnote↵next
    Every step of the loop has a single key and every key is printed on the control it triggers. A path that requires the mouse is a path that costs the agent a full second of hand travel, 78 times.
    6 · Never celebrate mid-block
    ✕ Confetti toast
    🎉
    Meeting booked! 4 to target!
    Steals 2s and the next call's opening
    ✓ Quiet confirmation
    Meeting booked · 16 Jul 11:00
    Next card already loading
    Gamification belongs on the between-blocks screen where it costs nothing. On the console it competes with a live human conversation, which it will always lose, or worse, win.

    Colour & contrast

    One brand hue, three functional hues, and a deliberate rule that separates them: green never means "good performance", it means "the line connected". Every pair below is a live sample with a meter.

    Token layers and naming

    Three layers. Screens only ever use the semantic layer, so a rebrand is one change at the primitive layer. Names are functional, never colours: element.tone.emphasis.state.

    1 · PrimitiveRaw values, no meaningviolet.500 = #7466D9stone.100 = #F3F0EBstone.950 = #141414

    What each hue is allowed to mean

    Brand · #7466D9

    Attention, not status. The one thing to do next, the current selection, the reason line.

    Rank 1
    Green · #10B981

    A human answered. Connect, live line, consent on file. Never used for targets or quota.

    ConnectedConsent
    Amber · #F59E0B

    Time-bound. A callback due, a calling window closing, a lead about to age out of its sequence.

    Callback dueCloses 18:00
    Red · #EF4444

    Blocked, and not by the agent. DNC, no consent, outside hours, suppressed. Never an error the agent caused.

    DNCOut of hours
    Colour-blind proofpasses
    ConnectedCallback 16:30Do not callNo answer
    ConnectedCallback 16:30Do not callNo answer
    Every outcome carries a word; blocking outcomes also carry a glyph. Strip the colour and the meaning survives, necessary because roughly 1 in 12 male agents has a colour-vision deficiency and outcome choice is the most-repeated action in the product.

    Mono is restricted to four things: the live call timer, the ring timer, call durations, and keyboard-shortcut keys. Everywhere else it is banned, a mono phone number or a mono lead name makes the console feel like a terminal, which is exactly the register we are avoiding.

    Phone numbers are grouped, never run together. +91 98450 12345 is read aloud by agents when confirming, so the grouping matches how it is spoken. Letter-spacing +0.02em, tabular figures, never truncated.

    Motion

    Everything below is running the real animation on a loop. Motion here has one job: make the card swap feel instant so the agent never waits between dials.

    Duration, three tokens travelling the same distance
    120ms
    micro
    Hover, focus ring, checkbox, disposition selection. Fast enough to feel caused by the key press.
    180ms
    standard
    Card swap, panel disclosure, toast, tooltip. The default, 20ms faster than a typical design system because it fires 78 times a day.
    260ms
    large
    Wrap panel rising, drawer, modal. Only for surfaces that cover more than half the centre column.
    There is no fourth duration and no entrance animation on the console. The next-call card cross-fades in 180ms; it does not slide, scale or stagger. A staggered entrance on a card the agent sees 78 times reads as a stutter by the tenth repetition.
    Easing, one curve
    cubic-bezier(.2, .8, .2, 1)

    Leaves fast, arrives slow, no overshoot. The dashed diagonal is linear for comparison.

    The card swap, running live
    Daniel Okafor
    Finance Lead · Brightline Logistics
    Callback he asked for, 16:30
    In at 180ms from the right, out at 180ms to the left, the direction encodes "forward through the queue". Reversing to a previous lead animates the opposite way, which is the only place direction carries meaning in this system.
    Ringing
    00:14
    The only rotational motion in the product. It stops the moment the line connects or the ring timer hits 22s.
    Live line
    04:12
    Pulse plus waveform means "audio is flowing". If the waveform flattens for 3s the agent knows the line dropped before the timer does.
    Quiet confirmation
    Meeting booked
    16 Jul 11:00 · invite sent
    3.5s dwell, bottom-left so it never covers the next-call card. No sound, no confetti, no counter increment.
    prefers-reduced-motion. The ring rotation stops and becomes a pulsing opacity; the card swap becomes a plain 100ms cross-fade; the waveform freezes at mid-height and the live dot alone carries the state. Nothing is removed, the agent still sees every state change.

    on the call bar the ring inverts to white @ 60%, indigo on ink is invisible
    The keyboard path is the primary path here, not a fallback. A focus ring that is hard to see is a defect of the same severity as a broken dial button.
    Never colour alone, four carriers on every outcome
    Do not call1 colour + 2 word + 3 glyph + 4 position (always the outcome slot)
    Do not callcolour removed, three carriers still standing
    ✕ bare dot, one carrier, and it is the one that fails
    The queue strip uses status dots for density, but every dot is paired with a word in its row. There is no bare coloured dot anywhere in Overhead.

    ① Brand + campaign

    Which list am I working? Agents switch campaigns between blocks and the wrong campaign is a real error, so the sequence name lives permanently under the wordmark.

    ② Availability status

    Ready · On a call · Wrap-up · Break · Offline. The only control the agent presses hourly. It also gates the queue, going to Break stops new cards arriving.

    ③ Identity + two numbers

    Name, pod and dials only. Not connects, not meetings, no bar. One neutral number is orientation; three coloured ones are a scoreboard.

    12

    Layout shells

    Seven arrangements, drawn as wireframes. Every screen in Overhead is one of these, and the console is the only one with three columns.

    L1 · Console3 + 6 + 3
    The calling screen. Queue left at 260, card centre, context right at 380. Call bar docks full width at the bottom when a call is live.
    L2 · Wrap overlayL1 + sheet
    Disposition & note. Rises over the centre and right columns only, the queue stays visible so the agent sees what is next while wrapping.
    L3 · Lead record8 + 4
    Lead, account, callback. Header with identity + score + next step, tab strip, activity left, facts right.
    L4 · Table12
    Lead lists · callbacks · call log · DNC registry. Sticky header, frozen name column, filters above.
    L5 · Dashboard4 × 3 then 8+4
    My numbers · floor · manager performance. KPI row then chart + list.
    L6 · Builder3 + 9
    Sequences · routing · DNC · settings. Nav left, editor right, sticky save.
    L0 · Barecentred 340
    Sign in · device check · shift start. No rail, no bar.
    There is no L7. Every request for an eighth shell so far has been the console with something added, which is the request the attention budget exists to refuse. If a screen does not fit one of these seven, it is usually a screen that should not exist.

    Selection controls

    Standard sizes, one non-standard rule: anything that changes what gets dialled uses a radio card with the consequence written on it.

    412 leads · 38 selected
    Radio cards, where the choice has a consequence
    What happens to the rest of this sequence?
    Pause until the callback
    No emails or calls until 18 Jul 16:30. She keeps her place in the sequence.
    Continue the sequence
    Email step 4 still goes out tomorrow. Use when the callback is a courtesy, not a commitment.
    End the sequence
    No further automated touches. She becomes a manual follow-up owned by you.
    A bare radio list would read "Pause / Continue / End" and mean nothing. The consequence sentence is the control, the radio is just the affordance.
    17

    Outcome & status badges

    Three densities and a strict vocabulary. Outcome is what happened on a call; status is what state a lead is in. They are different objects and they never share a shape.

    Anatomy across three sizes
    7Called7
    19px tall · sm · in-row
    9Connected9
    23px tall · md · default
    125Connected · 3:1212
    29px tall · lg · record header
    Radius is 6 (sm 5, lg 8), square-ish, not pill. A pill badge in this product would be confused with the chips, which are removable. Weight is always 600.
    The seven outcomes, the closed set
    1Interested→ books a meeting or a next call
    2Not now→ requires a callback date
    3Not a fit→ requires a reason from a list
    4Voicemail left→ advances the sequence one step
    5No answer→ retries at a different hour
    6Wrong number→ suppresses the number, keeps the lead
    7Do not call→ permanent, writes to the DNC registry
    Seven, and adding an eighth requires removing one. Every outcome maps to a number key, and seven is the practical ceiling for a keyboard grid. Sub-reasons live one level down (a "Not a fit" reason list) rather than expanding the top set, this is how the disposition step stays under 20 seconds.
    Lead status vs call outcome vs filter chip, three different jobs
    Outcome, what happened on one call
    InterestedVoicemail
    Filled square badge. Belongs to a call record, never to the lead. Appears in the activity timeline and the call log.
    Status, what state the lead is in now
    In sequence · step 3 of 6Callback due 16:30Paused, out of hours
    Dot plus words, no fill. There are 34 of these in a queue and 34 filled badges would be unreadable.
    Chip, a filter the agent applied
    PuneCallbacks only
    Outlined, removable, rounded 7. This is the agent's own doing, not the system reporting.

    Ordered by volume, not by desirability. Sorting a stacked bar by "good to bad" makes it look like a progress bar and invites the wrong reading.

    Each stage shows its rate against the stage above, never against the top. 11 of 389 is a demoralising number and a useless one; 35% of qualified conversations is a number a coach can work with.

    28

    Alerts, toasts & interruption

    A four-level ladder, and one rule that governs all of it: nothing interrupts a live call. Everything that arrives during a conversation is queued and delivered at wrap.

    The ladder, four levels, drawn
    Level 1
    Sequence paused until 18 Jul
    Inline · no dismiss · lives inside the thing it describes
    Level 2
    Callback scheduled
    Daniel Okafor · 16 Jul 10:00 WAT
    Toast · bottom-left · 3.5s · 8s undo window
    Level 3
    Your headset dropped to the laptop mic
    Call quality will be poor. Reconnect before the next dial.
    Banner · persists until resolved · never over a live call
    Level 4
    Campaign stopped by compliance
    SMB Payroll · 6-touch has been suspended. Your queue is empty until it resumes.
    Modal · blocks · requires acknowledgement · logged
    Level 4 is used four times in the whole product: campaign suspended, DNC confirmation, session expiry with unsaved wrap, and a telephony outage. Every other message is level 1 or 2.
    During a call, everything is held
    02:41Priya Raghavan2 held
    Meeting invite accepted, Tom Whelan
    Callback due in 9 minutes, Daniel Okafor
    The two messages exist but are not rendered. A small neutral counter on the call bar says how many are waiting; it is the only acknowledgement of them during the conversation.
    At wrap, delivered as a stack
    Meeting invite accepted, Tom Whelan
    Callback due in 9 minutes, Daniel Okafor
    Maximum three stacked; beyond that they collapse into "5 updates" with a link. The stack clears when the agent dials again.
    What is allowed to reach the agent at all
    EventLevelDuring a call
    Callback due in 10 min2 · toastHeld
    Meeting accepted2 · toastHeld
    Lead replied to an email2 · toastHeld
    Headset disconnected3 · bannerShown, affects this call
    Network degraded3 · bannerShown, affects this call
    Campaign suspended4 · modalHeld until wrap
    Lead added to DNC3 · bannerHeld until wrap
    Shift ending in 10 min1 · inlineHeld
    New coaching note1 · badgeHeld to block end
    Only three things can appear during a conversation, and all three are about the conversation itself. This table is the spec, anything not on it is held.

    Empty, loading & error states

    Six states, all drawn. In a calling tool an empty state is rarely "nothing here", it is usually "you cannot call right now", and it must say why and what happens next.

    Queue empty, block over
    Block finished
    41 dials · 9 connects · 2 meetings. Block 4 opens at 16:15 with 38 leads.
    Queue empty, nothing dialable
    Everyone is out of hours
    All 22 remaining leads are outside their calling window. The first opens at 08:00 IST, that is 34 minutes.
    No results, search
    No lead matches "98450 99"
    Searching name, phone, company and lead ID across all campaigns you can see.
    Loading, never blocking
    Skeleton mirrors the real card's geometry to the pixel. Rare in practice, the next card is prefetched during the current call.
    Error, recoverable
    Could not load the next lead
    Your connection dropped for a moment. Your last wrap was saved.
    ERR-QUEUE-503 · 15:46:22
    Error, call failed
    The line did not connect
    Carrier rejected the call. This is not counted as an attempt and Priya keeps her place in the sequence.
    31

    Modals, drawers & sheets

    Three overlay types with three different jobs. The wrap panel is a sheet, not a modal, and that distinction is load-bearing.

    Sheet, rises from below
    Wrap-up. Covers the centre and right columns, leaves the queue visible. 260ms up, 180ms down. No scrim, the console behind it is still information, not decoration.
    Drawer, slides from the right
    History · lead record preview · coaching notes. 420px, covers the context column. Esc closes. Never contains a primary action.
    Modal, centred, blocks
    Four uses only (§28). 480px, scrim at 42%, Esc cancels, focus trapped. Never used for anything the agent does routinely.

    Content

    Words are part of the interface: the terms, labels and tone every screen uses.43 Content & terminology
    43

    Content & terminology

    The words are part of the design. A telesales product that calls people "records" will be built by people who forget there is a human on the other end of the line.

    The vocabulary, say this, not that
    UseNeverBecause
    LeadRecord, prospect, target"Target" is how a floor starts talking about people
    CallContact attempt, touchAgents say "call"; the UI should too
    ConnectedSuccessful contactA voicemail is not a failure
    OutcomeDisposition (in the UI)Industry jargon; "How did it go?" is the label
    Not a fitUnqualified, junk, rejectedThe lead did nothing wrong
    Do not callBlacklist, blockedIt is a request from a person, stated plainly
    Their timeLocal time, TZWhose time is the whole point
    SequenceOverhead (in the UI)Overhead is the product; using it twice confuses
    Up nextQueue, worklist, my list"List" invites working top to bottom
    BlockSession, shift segmentWhat agents already call it
    DialsActivity, productivityA count, not a judgement
    WrapACW, after-call workCall-centre acronyms belong in reports
    Voice, four rules with examples
    1 · Second person, about a person
    ✕ High propensity · intent signal detected
    ✓ She opened your pricing page twice yesterday
    2 · State the time, not "soon"
    ✕ Outside calling hours. Try again later.
    ✓ 21:14 in Pune. She can be called from 09:00 · that is 11 hours.
    3 · Never blame the agent for the system
    ✕ Invalid action. This lead cannot be dialled.
    ✓ Priya asked not to be called, at 09:12 today. Nothing you did.
    4 · No exclamation marks, ever
    ✕ Great job! Meeting booked! 🎉
    ✓ Meeting booked · Thu 16 Jul 11:00 · invite sent
    Number, date and time formats
    ThingFormatExampleNote
    Their local timeHH:MM + zone15:42 IST24-hour, zone always named
    Live call timerMM:SS mono04:12Leading zero kept so width never changes
    Call duration in a listM:SS mono3:12No leading zero once the call is over
    Date, this yearDD MMM16 JulYear added only when it differs
    Date + timeDD MMM HH:MM16 Jul 11:00Always the lead's zone when it is about them
    Relative timeunder 24h onlyin 9 min · 2h agoBeyond that, an absolute date
    Phonegrouped as spoken+91 98450 12345Never truncated on the console
    Currencysymbol + lakh grouping₹ 1,84,000Per the account's country
    Percentagesone decimal18.4%Whole numbers only above 100 samples
    Countsplain41 dialsNever "41/78" without the word

      01For vibe coders

      Every AI tool, one style

      You prompt Cursor, Lovable and Claude all day. Each one invents a new look. Paste one brief and they all build the same product.

      • Purple gradients and emoji iconsYour brand, every screen
      • Re-prompting to fix spacingRight the first time
      • Three tools, three stylesOne brief, one system
      What you can do
      1. Pick your brand colour, radius and look on the home page.
      2. Download SKILL.md or copy the brief, then add it to Claude, Cursor or Lovable once.
      3. Ask for screens in plain words. They come back with your tokens, Overhead components and sentence-case copy.
      4. Run the audit on any screen to see what drifted and get the fix.

      02For designers

      The whole system in Figma

      Import one file and publish it as a library. Every component, variable and text style is ready to drag into the screens you are already designing.

      • Rebuilding a kit from screenshotsThe real file, one import
      • Detached copies everywhereA published library
      • Values that drift from codeThe same tokens as React
      What you can do
      1. Import overhead-design-system.fig into your Figma workspace.
      2. Publish it as a library; every page becomes a section in Assets.
      3. Drag in components and switch variants from the properties panel. Light and dark switch with one mode change.
      4. Hand off with the same names developers import: Button, Input field, Chart.

      03For developers

      Install, import, ship

      Install overhead-ui and import the same components the designers use. Every value is a token, so what you ship matches the Figma file to the pixel.

      • Eyeballing values from FigmaExact tokens in code
      • Rebuilding the same buttonImport it once
      • A redesign means a rewriteChange one hex
      What you can do
      1. Run npm install overhead-ui in your project folder.
      2. Add the stylesheet and OverheadProvider once in your root file.
      3. Import components by the Figma names. Props are the Figma properties in camelCase.
      4. Rebrand by changing CSS variables; every component follows. Charts use the same geometry as the Figma file.

      04For teams & agencies

      One system, every client

      Every client gets their own look. Your team keeps one way of building: the same spacing, type rules and components underneath.

      • A new kit for every clientOne kit, many themes
      • Handoffs that driftShared tokens
      • Week-long setupTheme in an afternoon
      What you can do
      1. Duplicate the style pack for each client and set their brand colour and radius.
      2. Keep one Figma library and one package; only the tokens change per client.
      3. Give each client team SKILL.md so their AI tools follow the same rules.
      4. Review work against one checklist instead of a new kit every time.
